title: Mormon’s Epistle
summary: Mormon’s people march before the Lamanites. Mormon writes to the Lamanite king, requesting that his people be allowed to gather at Cumorah for battle; the king grants the request.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says his record concerns the destruction of the Nephites and that his people marched forth before the Lamanites.
Mormon wrote an epistle asking the Lamanite king to let the Nephites gather at Cumorah for battle.
The Lamanite king granted Mormon’s request.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon writing an epistle can be depicted with a writing surface and implement.
unspecified_visual_details: The epistle’s appearance and writing materials.
The appearance of the Lamanite king and the location where the epistle is written or received.

narration.text: And now I finish my record concerning the destruction of my people, the Nephites.
And I, Mormon, wrote an epistle unto the king of the Lamanites
did grant unto me the thing which I desired.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Lamanite king in the same location as Mormon unless depicting the separate grant as its own moment.
Do not invent the text of the epistle.

title: Gathering at Cumorah
summary: The Nephites march to Cumorah, camp around the hill, and gather the remainder of their people there.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites marched to Cumorah and pitched tents around the hill in a land of many waters, rivers, and fountains; they hoped to gain an advantage.
After 384 years had passed, the remainder of the Nephites had gathered at Cumorah.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Tents around the hill and nearby watercourses can be shown.
unspecified_visual_details: The arrangement and design of the tents.

narration.text: we did pitch our tents around about the hill Cumorah
we had gathered in all the remainder of our people unto the land of Cumorah.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle in this gathering scene.

title: The Records Hidden
summary: As the gathered people face their last struggle, old Mormon makes a record from the plates of Nephi, hides the entrusted records in Cumorah, and gives a few plates to Moroni.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon had grown old, knew this was his people’s last struggle, and had been commanded not to let the sacred records fall into Lamanite hands.
Mormon made a record from the plates of Nephi, hid the entrusted records in Cumorah except for a few plates, and gave those few plates to his son Moroni.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon can be shown handling plates and concealing records in the hill; Moroni can be shown receiving the few plates.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise place and method of concealment within the hill.
The appearance and material of the plates.

narration.text: I made this record out of the plates of Nephi
and hid up in the hill Cumorah all the records
which I gave unto my son Moroni.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Lamanites discovering the records.
Do not depict the Lord as visibly present; no appearance is described.

title: The Lamanite Armies Approach
summary: The narrator’s people, with their wives and children, see the Lamanite armies marching toward them and await their arrival in fear. The armies come to battle, and every soul is filled with terror at their numbers.
characters: The narrator’s people, including their wives and children

explicit_facts.text: The narrator’s people, with their wives and children, saw the Lamanite armies marching toward them and awaited them in fear.
The armies came to battle against the narrator’s people, and every soul was filled with terror because of their numbers.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The approaching armies can be shown at a distance while the narrator’s people watch.
unspecified_visual_details: The armies’ clothing, equipment, and exact size.

narration.text: did now behold the armies of the Lamanites marching towards them
they came to battle against us

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The description of fear filling breasts is figurative, not a visible entity.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict fear as a supernatural figure.
Do not invent combat actions, injuries, or dialogue.

title: The Attack
summary: Attackers fall upon the narrator's people with weapons of war. The narrator's men are cut down, and the narrator falls wounded. The attackers pass without ending the narrator's life.

explicit_facts.text: Attackers fell upon the narrator's people with swords, bows, arrows, axes, and other weapons of war.
The narrator's men, including ten thousand who were with the narrator, were cut down.
The narrator fell wounded in their midst, and the attackers passed by without ending the narrator's life.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The described combat and the narrator's fall can be shown without visible wounds or gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The combatants' appearances, weapon designs, and precise setting are not specified.

narration.text: they did fall upon my people with the sword, and with the bow, and with the arrow, and with the ax, and with all manner of weapons of war.
my men were hewn down, yea, even my ten thousand who were with me, and I fell wounded in the midst; and they passed by me that they did not put an end to my life.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Do not reconstruct events from verses outside those supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the attackers, the narrator's people, or the location by names absent from the supplied verses.
Do not show blood, exposed wounds, or severed body parts.
Do not imply the narrator was killed.

title: The Survivors Look from Cumorah
summary: On the morrow, after the Lamanites have returned to their camps, Mormon and the other survivors, including his son Moroni, look from the top of the hill Cumorah and behold the ten thousand of Mormon’s people led by him and the ten thousand led by Moroni, all hewn down.

explicit_facts.text: Twenty-four of Mormon’s people survived, including Mormon’s son Moroni.
On the morrow, after the Lamanites returned to their camps, the survivors beheld from the top of hill Cumorah the ten thousand of Mormon’s people who had been led by him and hewn down.
The survivors also beheld the ten thousand of Mormon’s people led by Moroni.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The survivors can be shown looking down from the hill at the fallen people, without visible gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The survivors’ clothing and exact positions.
The terrain and the precise arrangement of the fallen people.

narration.text: from the top of the hill Cumorah
And we also beheld the ten thousand of my people who were led by my son Moroni.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the battle continuing; the view occurs on the morrow after the Lamanites have returned to their camps.
Do not add survivors, escapees, deserters, or named fallen leaders not identified in the supplied verses.
Do not show wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: The Fallen Tens of Thousands
summary: Gidgiddonah and his ten thousand had fallen. The account names ten others who had fallen and reports ten more who fell by the sword. Nearly all the narrator’s people had fallen, except the twenty-four with him, a few who escaped into the south countries, and a few who deserted to the Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: Gidgiddonah’s ten thousand had fallen, and he had fallen among them.
Lamah, Gilgal, Limhah, and Jeneum had each fallen with his ten thousand.
Cumenihah, Moronihah, Antionum, Shiblom, Shem, and Josh are named together as having fallen with their ten thousand each.
Ten more fell by the sword with their ten thousand each.
All the narrator’s people had fallen except the twenty-four with him, a few who escaped into the south countries, and a few who deserted to the Lamanites.
The remains of the fallen were left upon the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A distant view of the aftermath can convey the scale of the losses without graphic detail.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearances of the named people and survivors.
The identities of those who escaped or deserted.

narration.text: And behold, the ten thousand of Gidgiddonah had fallen, and he also in the midst.
yea, even all my people, save it were those twenty and four who were with me,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses report losses and exceptions; they do not describe a new gathering or encounter among the survivors.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign an exact location or depict this aftermath at Cumorah based on these verses.
Do not depict the named fallen people alive or give them invented biographies.
Do not show wounds, blood, severed body parts, or graphic decomposition.
Do not stage the escape south or desertion as part of this aftermath scene.

title: A Lament for the Slain
summary: Anguished because his people have been slain, the narrator cries out and mourns their fall and loss.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator is anguished because his people have been slain, and he cries out.
He asks how those he addresses departed from the ways of the Lord and rejected Jesus.
He mourns their fall and loss.
He addresses sons and daughters, fathers and mothers, and husbands and wives.
He says his sorrows cannot bring them back.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The narrator may appear grief-stricken as he cries out.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the narrator’s appearance, and whether the slain are visible.

spoken_dialogue.text: O ye fair ones, how could ye have departed from the ways of the Lord!
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The lamenting narrator

spoken_dialogue.text: O ye fair ones, how could ye have rejected that Jesus, who stood with open arms to receive you!
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The lamenting narrator

spoken_dialogue.text: But behold, ye are fallen, and I mourn your loss.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The lamenting narrator

spoken_dialogue.text: But behold, ye are gone, and my sorrows cannot bring your return.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The lamenting narrator

narration.text: my soul was rent with anguish

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The reference to Jesus standing with open arms occurs in the lament; these verses do not narrate his visible appearance.
The verses do not specify where the lament takes place.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Jesus appearing or turn the reference to his open arms into a visible event.
Do not invent intervening events, a setting, or identities for the slain.

title: Mormon’s Words of Judgment and Hope
summary: Mormon speaks of the dead rising to immortality and standing before Christ’s judgment seat, and laments that they did not repent before the destruction. He says the Eternal Father knows their state and acts according to justice and mercy.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says the dead will put on immortality, their bodies become incorruptible, and they will stand before Christ’s judgment seat to be judged according to their works.
Mormon says the righteous will be blessed with their fathers, and laments that the people did not repent before the destruction.
Mormon says the Eternal Father knows their state and acts according to justice and mercy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may continue speaking at the hill; no additional event is narrated.
unspecified_visual_details: Any appearance of Christ, the judgment seat, or the dead in a future state.

spoken_dialogue.text: O that ye had repented before this great destruction had come upon you.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Mormon

narration.text: these bodies which are now moldering in corruption must soon become incorruptible bodies
the Father, yea, the Eternal Father of heaven, knoweth your state

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The resurrection and judgment are spoken of as future teachings, not shown as present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict resurrection, judgment, or a visible divine figure.
